rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human embodiment develops from semen mixed with menstrual blood, both deriving from food made from the four elements; their hot, cold, moist, and dry qualities interact into a balanced temperament ready for governing powers.
rows.anchor: بدن الإنسان إنما يتولد عند امتزاج المني بدم الطمث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plant powers attract, retain, digest, and expel food, replace what is lost, grow the organs, and leave surplus material for reproduction.
rows.anchor: قوى نباتية وهي التي تجذب الغذاء ، ثم تمسكه ثم تهضمه ثم تدفع الفضلة المؤذية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animal powers include perception through the senses, imagination, memory, and recollection, plus active powers such as appetite and anger and the forces operating in the muscles.
rows.anchor: قوى حيوانية بعضها مدركة كالحواس الخمس والخيال والحفظ والذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human powers are intellectual and practical; the intellectual powers apprehend realities in spiritual and bodily, higher and lower realms.
rows.anchor: ومنها قوى إنسانية وهي إما مدركة أو عاملة ، والقوى المدركة هي القوى القوية على إدراك حقائق الأشياء الروحانية والجسمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every component of the bodily world has things that suit and complete it and things that oppose and harm it, along with powers that attract the fitting and repel the harmful; well-being therefore requires creation and guidance.
rows.anchor: وجدت لها أشياء تلائمها وتكمل حالها وأشياء تنافرها وتفسد حالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation means bringing the person into existence, while guidance means the powers that draw benefits and repel harms, so the phrase gathers worldly and religious benefits.
rows.anchor: أما الخلق فبتصييره موجودا بعد أن كان معدوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation is phrased in the past because the self is created once, whereas guidance is phrased in the present because divine direction recurs continually through worldly and religious benefits.
rows.anchor: أما هدايته تعالى فهي مما يتكرر كل حين وأوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly guidance lets the senses distinguish benefit from harm; religious guidance lets reason distinguish truth from falsehood and good from evil at every moment.
rows.anchor: وذلك بأن تحكم الحواس بتمييز المنافع عن المضار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Food and drink represent every beneficial provision: food alone would not complete the blessing without appetite, strength, and discrimination that enable eating and nourishment.
rows.anchor: من أكله والاغتذاء به نحو الشهوة والقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham says when he is ill rather than saying God made him ill because people often cause illness through negligence in food, drink, and other habits; the sages quip that most dead people would blame indigestion.
rows.anchor: بتفريط من الإنسان في مطاعمه ومشاربه

rows.speaker: الحكماء
rows.claim: The sages say that if most dead people were asked what caused their deaths, they would answer that it was indigestion.
rows.anchor: قالت الحكماء : لو قيل لأكثر الموتى ما سبب آجالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illness comes from one humor overpowering another through their natural aversion; health and recovery require a coercive force to reunite and balance them, so healing is attributed to God rather than illness.
rows.anchor: ما بينها من التنافر الطبيعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Healing is beloved and a foundational blessing, whereas illness is disliked and not a blessing; Abraham lists blessings, so he does not attribute illness to God. Death is not itself harmful without sensation, its harmful preliminaries are illness, and release can be happiness for perfected souls.
rows.anchor: الشفاء محبوب وهو من أصول النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dying means release from worldly afflictions and punishments, and being brought back to life means receiving recompense.
rows.anchor: الإماتة في الدنيا والتخلص عن آفاتها وعقوباتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham hopes for forgiveness as every rational person seeks escape from punishment and attainment of reward.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما هو مطلوب كل عاقل من الخلاص عن العذاب والفوز بالثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's words encompass all God's blessings from the beginning of creation through the everlasting afterlife.
rows.anchor: جمع في هذه الألفاظ جميع نعم الله تعالى من أول الخلق إلى آخر الأبد في الدار الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording of hope is appropriate because, on Razi's doctrine, God owes no one anything, may do what He wills, and no one can object to His acts.
rows.anchor: حيث قلنا إنه لا يجب على الله لأحد شيء

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says the clause refers to all believers, who hope for forgiveness without certainty.
rows.anchor: أراد به سائر المؤمنين لأنهم الذين يطمعون ولا يقطعون به

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The alternative that hope means certainty is reported from al-Hasan.
rows.anchor: المراد من الطمع اليقين ، وهو مروي عن الحسن

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says Abraham used this wording to teach his community how to supplicate.
rows.anchor: وأجاب صاحب ( الكشاف ) : بأنه إنما ذكره على هذا الوجه تعليما منه لأمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the first answer because the passage narrates Abraham's praise and then prayer as one continuous speech, so assigning this clause to someone else breaks its coherence.
rows.anchor: ومن أول المدح إلى آخر الدعاء كلام إبراهيم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects taking hope to mean certainty because that is contrary to Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: وهو أن الطمع هو اليقين فهذا على خلاف اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the teaching explanation because it would mean Abraham falsely spoke about himself for instructional purposes.
rows.anchor: فباطل أيضا لأن حاصله يرجع إلى أنه كذب على نفسه لغرض تعليم الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed explanation says Abraham's sin was lying in saying the great idol acted, that he was sick, and that Sarah was his sister; Razi rejects it because lying cannot be ascribed to a prophet.
rows.anchor: محمول على كذب إبراهيم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation treats the confession as humility, but Razi rejects it: if truthful it leaves the problem unresolved, and if false it makes sin the means of denying sin.
rows.anchor: ذكره على سبيل التواضع وهضم النفس وهذا ضعيف لأنه إن كان صادقا في هذا التواضع فقد لزم الإشكال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's correct answer is that خطيئة means leaving the better course, which may be called an error and is permissible for prophets; selling a valuable gem for a dinar illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: الجواب الصحيح أن يحمل ذلك على ترك الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although forgiveness can occur in worldly life, its effect appears on Judgment Day and remains hidden now.
rows.anchor: لأن أثرها يظهر يوم الدين وهو الآن خفي لا يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for me means God's forgiveness benefits the forgiven person alone: human pardon often seeks reward, avoidance, praise, or relief from compassion, but God is perfect and cannot gain a new perfection or lose a defect.
rows.anchor: لم يكن المقصود من ذلك العفو رعاية جانب المعفو عنه بل رعاية جانب نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation says Abraham was created for God's sake despite not yet existing and being unable to benefit God; forgiveness for his sake is therefore more fitting when he needs it most.
rows.anchor: خلقتني لا لي فإنك حين خلقتني ما كنت موجودا وإذا لم أكن موجودا استحال تحصيل شيء لأجلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation ties the request to Abraham's absorption in knowledge of God and aversion to intermediaries: he seeks forgiveness through his own servitude and need, not an intercessor.
rows.anchor: لشدة استغراقه في بحر المعرفة شديد الفرار عن الالتفات إلى الوسائط

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: When Gabriel asked whether he had a need, Abraham replied that he had no need of Gabriel, illustrating his refusal to turn to intermediaries.
rows.anchor: ألك حاجة ؟ قال أما إليك فلا

none: The segment contains only a continuation slash and no source explanation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage first recounts Abraham praising God and then his prayer, teaching that praise should precede supplication.
rows.anchor: تقديم الثناء على الدعاء من المهمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human souls resemble angels when occupied with knowledge and love of God and drawn toward spiritual realities; this kinship makes them more capable of acting upon bodily nature.
rows.anchor: كلما كان اشتغالها بمعرفة الله تعالى ومحبته والانجذاب إلى عالم الروحانيات أشد كانت مشاكلتها للملائكة أتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Absorption in worldly pleasures and bodily darkness makes souls resemble beasts, leaving them weaker and less influential in the world.
rows.anchor: كلما كان اشتغالها بلذات هذا العالم واستغراقها في ظلمات هذه الجسمانيات أشد كانت مشاكلتها للبهائم أشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praising God's greatness before asking immerses the supplicant in knowledge and love, makes the soul more angelic, and thereby prepares a celestial power that brings the requested thing into being; Razi calls this a duty of supplication.
rows.anchor: بسبب ذلك الذكر يصير مستغرقا في معرفة الله ومحبته ويصير قريب المشاكلة من الملائكة فتحصل له بسبب تلك المشاكلة قوة إلهية سماوية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report in which the Prophet quotes God says that whoever is occupied by remembrance rather than asking will receive more than the supplicants receive.
rows.anchor: من شغله ذكري عن مسألتي أعطيته أفضل ما أعطي السائلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham did not restrict himself to praise while teaching people the true religion: he rejected their gods, praised God, then prayed; a preacher must teach the religious practice.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر الثناء ، ثم ذكر الدعاء لأن الشارع لا بد له من تعليم الشرع

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: A report says Abraham, when alone and not teaching religious practice, would suffice with saying that God's knowledge of his state was enough in place of asking.
rows.anchor: كان يقتصر على قوله : حسبي من سؤالي علمه بحالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's request not to be humiliated supports the view that God is not obligated to anyone, as argued under 26:82.
rows.anchor: يدل على أنه لا يجب على الله تعالى شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Abraham already asked to inherit Paradise, and the verse says humiliation belongs to unbelievers, an infallible prophet may fear the humiliation appropriate to his own rank: the righteous person's merits can be failings for the intimate, and their degrees can be abysses for the intimate.
rows.anchor: حسنات الأبرار سيئات المقربين فكذا درجات الأبرار دركات المقربين وخزي كل واحد بما يليق به

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the subject pronoun in they are raised refers either to the servants, understood from context, or to the erring people.
rows.anchor: في ( يبعثون ) ضمير العباد لأنه معلوم أو ضمير الضالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God honored Abraham with the description of a sound heart, also used of Abraham in 37:83–84.
rows.anchor: أكرمه بهذا الوصف حيث قال : { وإن من شيعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes the exception a replacement: asked whether Zayd has wealth and sons, one answers that his wealth and sons are soundness of heart, denying the possessions and affirming the heart instead.
rows.anchor: تريد نفي المال والبنين عنه وإثبات سلامة القلب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parsing takes wealth and sons to mean worldly affluence: only the religious wealth of a person with a sound heart benefits, as worldly wealth consists in possessions and children.
rows.anchor: نجعل المال والبنين في معنى الغنى كأنه قيل يوم لا ينفع غنى إلا غنى من أتى الله بقلب سليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parsing makes the exception the object of benefits: wealth and sons help only a person whose heart is sound, who spends wealth in obedience and guides children to religion; the heart is also free from their temptation.
rows.anchor: رجلا سلم قلبه مع ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound heart most correctly means freedom from ignorance and vile traits: just as bodily health is the proper constitution and illness its loss, the heart needs knowledge and excellent character and must be free of false beliefs and worldly desires.
rows.anchor: وهو الأصح أن المراد منه سلامة القلب عن الجهل والأخلاق الرذيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says that if a sound heart suffices for salvation, the tongue and limbs need no soundness; Razi answers that the heart governs and the limbs follow, so their failure proves the heart is unsound.
rows.anchor: أن القلب مؤثر واللسان والجوارح تبع فلو كان القلب سليما لكانا سليمين لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation says sound means bitten, in fear of God.
rows.anchor: أن السليم هو اللديغ من خشية الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation understands sound as the one who is safe, submits, yields, and surrenders.
rows.anchor: أن السليم هو الذي سلم وأسلم وسالم واستسلم

none: The segment contains only quoted Qur’anic text and no source explanation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After showing that the heavens, earth, and what lies between depend on a governor, the verse says even the greatest bodies are created and owned, proving God's unsurpassed power and lordship.
rows.anchor: لما بين افتقار السموات والأرض وما بينهما إلى المدبر ذكر بعد ذلك أن ما هو أعظم الأجسام فهي مخلوقة ومربوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes differ on whether the words from I have encompassed through the mighty are spoken by the hoopoe or by the Lord of might.
rows.anchor: قيل من { أحطت } إلى { العظيم } كلام الهدهد وقيل كلام رب العزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration of recitation is obligatory in both readings, as Shafi'i and Abu Hanifa hold: the consensus count is fourteen and this is one, while one reading commands prostration and the other censures its omission; Razi rejects al-Zajjaj's position limiting obligation to the light reading.
rows.anchor: الحق أن سجدة التلاوة واجبة في القراءتين جميعا وهو قول الشافعي وأبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says prostration is obligatory with the light reading but not the doubled reading; Razi rejects this because one reading commands prostration and the other blames its omission.
rows.anchor: الذي ذكره الزجاج من وجوب السجدة مع التخفيف دون التشديد غير ملتفت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pausing differs by reading: with the light reading, one may stop at they do not find guidance and begin with whether they prostrate, or stop at whether and begin prostrate; with the doubled reading one pauses only at the mighty throne.
rows.anchor: نعم إذا خفف وقف على { فهم لا يهتدون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We shall see means that Solomon will consider the matter, that is, whether the hoopoe told the truth or lied; calling him among the liars is stronger because a known liar is already suspect and untrustworthy.
rows.anchor: فمن النظر الذي هو التأمل ، وأراد صدقت أم كذبت إلا أن { أم كنت من الكاذبين } أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to deliver it to them uses the plural because the hoopoe had found the queen and her people worshipping the sun, so the group is intended.
rows.anchor: أي إلى الذين هذا دينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away means withdrawing to a nearby concealed place so Solomon can hear their response; return is used in the sense of people answering one another, as in 34:30.
rows.anchor: و { يرجعون } من قوله تعالى : { يرجع بعضهم إلى بعض القول } ( سبأ : 30 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also said that the hoopoe entered by an opening, dropped the letter to the queen, and concealed himself in that opening.
rows.anchor: ويقال دخل عليها من كوة وألقى إليها الكتاب وتوارى في الكوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen's statement that a letter was delivered to her implicitly omits the hoopoe as the one who threw it to her.
rows.anchor: بمعنى أن يقال إن الهدهد ألقى إليها الكتاب فهو محذوف كأنه ثابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says the queen locked the doors while sleeping, put the keys under her head, and the hoopoe entered through an opening and laid the letter on her chest; another says he pecked her awake and startled her.
rows.anchor: كانت إذا رقدت غلقت الأبواب ووضعت المفاتيح تحت رأسها فدخل من كوة وطرح الكتاب على نحرها وهي مستلقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter is called noble because its contents are good, because it came from a noble king, or because it was sealed.
rows.anchor: أحدها : حسن مضمونه وما فيه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic saying states that a letter's nobility lies in its being sealed.
rows.anchor: كرم الكتاب ختمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Solomon wrote to non-Arabs and, after being told they accepted only sealed letters, adopted a signet ring.
rows.anchor: فقيل له إنهم لا يقبلون إلا كتابا عليه خاتم فاتخذ لنفسه خاتما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen's words identify and explain the letter she has just called noble, as though she were answering who sent it and what it said.
rows.anchor: أنه استئناف وتبيين لما ألقى إليها كأنها لما قالت إني ألقي إلي كتاب كريم

rows.speaker: عبدالله
rows.claim: Abdullah reads the clause as coordinated with the queen's preceding statement I have received.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبدالله { إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a reading with the two inna clauses opened, one analysis makes the statement an apposition to letter, as if what was delivered was that it came from Solomon.
rows.anchor: أنه بدل من كتاب كأنه قيل ألقي إلي أنه من سليمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis understands the clause as saying it is from Solomon and because it begins in God's name, with the basmala explaining its nobility.
rows.anchor: أن يريد أن من سليمان ولأنه بسم الله كأنها عللت كرمه بكونه من سليمان وتصديره بسم الله

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy reads أن من سليمان وأن بسم الله, taking the particles as explanatory; the أن in ألا تعلوا is also explanatory.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي ( أن من سليمان وأن بسم الله ) على أن المفسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not exalt yourselves means do not be arrogant as kings are.
rows.anchor: ومعنى لا تعلوا لا تتكبروا كما تفعل الملوك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the verb with ghayn, from excess or transgression beyond the limit.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس بالغين معجمة من الغلو وهي مجاوزة الحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon did not put his own name before the basmala: he began with the basmala, while the queen first identified the letter as his and then quoted its contents, so the order belongs to her report.
rows.anchor: حاشاه من ذلك بل ابتدأ هو ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets write concisely and address only what is needed: people need knowledge before action, and the basmala establishes God as existent, knowing, powerful, living, willing, wise, and merciful.
rows.anchor: الأنبياء عليهم السلام لا يطيلون بل يقتصرون على المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on exalting oneself prohibits following the ego and its desires as well as arrogance.
rows.anchor: نهي عن الانقياد لطاعة النفس والهوى والتكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslim can mean obedient and compliant, or it can mean a believer; the concise letter therefore contains what is needed for religion and worldly life.
rows.anchor: فالمراد من المسلم إما المنقاد أو المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order to submit before proving Solomon's messengership does not rely on blind imitation: the hoopoe's message is a miracle proving God, His attributes, and the claimant's truth, so no further proof was needed in the letter.
rows.anchor: المعجز يدل على وجود الصانع وعلى صفاته ويدل على صدق المدعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatwa means an answer to a new case, metaphorically derived from a young person; the queen asks for their judgment about her affair to please them and learn their view.
rows.anchor: الفتوى هي الجواب في الحادثة اشتقت على طريق الاستعارة من الفتى في السن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By saying she would not decide an affair without them, the queen means she will decide only in their presence.
rows.anchor: إلا بمحضركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their strength means bodily power and the strength of equipment and numbers; their battle prowess means courage and steadfastness in war.
rows.anchor: المراد قوة الأجسام وقوة الآلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The advisers display their natural and acquired strength to show they can fight if she chooses defense, then say the decision is hers to show obedience if she chooses peace; Razi calls it the best possible reply.
rows.anchor: إظهار القوة الذاتية والعرضية ليظهر أنها إن أرادتهم للدفع والحرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their final offer that the decision rests with the queen expresses their obedience to her command.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك إظهار الطاعة لها إن أرادت السلم

none: The segment contains only a continuation slash and no source explanation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question whether they are rewarded except for what they did may use a shift in address, or may quote what is said to them as they are cast down, with the verb of saying omitted.
rows.anchor: وحكاية ما يقال لهم عند الكب بإضمار القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conclusion follows the discussion of creation, return, prophethood, the preliminaries of Judgment, and its people's reward and punishment, completing the presentation of the foundations of religion.
rows.anchor: وذلك كمال ما يتعلق ببيان أصول الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first command is to worship God alone; after presenting proofs of monotheism, Muhammad can say those proofs convinced him, and he remains firm whether his audience accepts or rejects them.
rows.anchor: أن أخص الله وحده بالعبادة ولا أتخذ له شريكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord of this town means Mecca, singled out as God's dearest and most honored land, the home of the Prophet and the place where revelation descended.
rows.anchor: المراد مكة وإنما اختصها من بين سائر البلاد بإضافة اسمه إليها لأنها أحب بلاده إليه وأكرمها عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading uses the feminine relative pronoun, which Razi explains through the town's sacred restrictions: pilgrims face prohibitions, refugees are safe, and its trees and game are protected.
rows.anchor: وإنما وصفها بالتحريم لوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs recognized Mecca's sanctity and knew the idols did not confer it; since God alone bestowed this blessing, worship must be directed to Him alone.
rows.anchor: لأن العرب كانوا معترفين بكون مكة محرمة وعلموا أن تلك الفضيلة ليست من الأصنام بل من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To say that everything belongs to God condenses the surah's earlier proofs of monotheism, especially that He created all blessings, like a ruler described after listing his powers as owner of the whole world.
rows.anchor: وهذا إشارة إلى ما تقدم من الدلائل المذكورة في هذه السورة على التوحيد من كونه تعالى خالقا لجميع النعم فأجمل ههنا تلك المفصلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was commanded to be among those who submit and to recite the Qur'an to the people, and he fulfilled both tasks fully.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أمر بأن يكون / من المسلمين الثالث : أمر بأن يتلو القرآن عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance in the three preceding matters, monotheism, resurrection, and prophethood, benefits the guided person; if someone strays, the Prophet has no responsibility beyond warning as a messenger.
rows.anchor: { فإنما يهتدى لنفسه } أي منفعة اهتدائه راجعة إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise to God may thank Him for granting knowledge, wisdom, and prophethood, or for enabling the Prophet to discharge the message and warn.
rows.anchor: على ما أعطاني من نعمة العلم والحكمة والنبوة أو على ما وفقني من القيام بأداء الرسالة وبالإنذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will show the audience His overwhelming signs, which they will recognize only when faith no longer benefits them.
rows.anchor: القاهرة { فتعرفونها } لكن حين لا ينفعكم الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not heedless because He will bring the workers their recompense.
rows.anchor: لأنه من وراء جزاء العاملين
